raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview
The gfx950 FP8 asm MLA prefill pads heads to a multiple of 16. When the target is a multiple of the real head count (8 → 16, e.g. Kimi-K2.x at TP8), `get_mla_padded_q` uses `repeat_interleave`, but the output was sliced back as `[:, :num_heads]`, which is only correct for tile padding. The model then attends with the wrong heads and produces garbage. Introduced by #51040.

## Claims
- Restores accuracy for interleave-padded head counts: Kimi-K2.6 MXFP4 TP8 GSM8K 0.027 → 0.933.
- No performance change: same kernels; the unpad copy is still one kernel at the same cost.
- Adds the 8-head (interleaved) case to `test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py`.

## Validation
Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4, TP8, MI355X, fp8 KV cache. GSM8K 5-shot, `lm_eval --model local-completions ... --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5`, num_concurrent=64:

| | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---|---|---|
| Before (upstream main) | 0.0273 ± 0.0045 | 0.0235 ± 0.0042 |
| After (this PR) | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 |

Torch profiler, random 1024/1024, 64 prompts, concurrency 64: 40 kernels per prefill MoE layer before and after.

Unit test on MI355X: `pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_aiter_mla_fp8_prefill.py`

| Code under test | Result |
|---|---|
| This PR | 12 passed |
| Upstream unpad, with the new test cases | 2 failed, 10 passed: only `test_fp8_prefill_matches_reference[128-8]` and `[512-8]` fail |

<details>
<summary>Failure details on the upstream unpad</summary>

- `[128-8]`: mismatched elements 81,670 / 131,072 (62.3%), greatest absolute difference 4.5 (atol 0.1)
- `[512-8]`: mismatched elements 230,240 / 524,288 (43.9%), greatest absolute difference 4.5 (atol 0.1)
- All tile-padded (12, 24) and unpadded (16) cases pass on both versions.
</details>

## Details
Real heads sit at stride `nhead // num_heads` after `repeat_interleave` and at `[0:num_heads]` after tiling; the fix selects accordingly. Existing test head counts (12, 16, 24) only exercised tile padding.
No duplicate: no open issue or PR addresses this; #59966 changes `get_mla_padded_q` but keeps `repeat_interleave` for the divisor case.
AI assistance was used to prepare this change and description; I reviewed every changed line.


---

- [X] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [X] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [ ] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.

files.patch:
@@ -47,16 +47,18 @@ def _fp8_prefill_available() -> bool:
 #
 # The kernel requires 16-aligned heads, so _mla_fp8_prefill_attn replicate-pads
 # q/k/v up to get_fp8_prefill_num_heads(num_heads) and slices the output back.
-# Cover all three regimes:
+# Cover all four regimes:
+#    8 -> padded to 16 (divisor, repeat_interleave), so the real heads sit at
+#         stride 2 in the padded output. Live case: Kimi-K2.x at TP8.
 #   12 -> padded to 16 (non-divisor, tile+slice). Live case: a K3 rank at TP8.
 #   16 -> no padding, output aliases the caller's buffer.
 #   24 -> padded to 32. No current model and TP reaches this band (96 heads
 #         would need TP4, which does not fit in 288 GiB; 128-head models give
 #         128/64/32/16/8), so this case exists to keep the general path honest
-#         for future architectures: it is the only one of the three where
-#         padding above 16 actually happens, so it is what proves the
-#         replicate-pad/slice-back argument holds for a target other than 16.
-HEAD_COUNTS = [12, 16, 24]
+#         for future architectures: it is the only one where padding above
+#         16 actually happens, so it is what proves the replicate-pad/slice-back
+#         argument holds for a target other than 16.
+HEAD_COUNTS = [8, 12, 16, 24]
 QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM = 128
 QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM = 64
 QK_HEAD_DIM = QK_NOPE_HEAD_DIM + QK_ROPE_HEAD_DIM  # 192

@@ -2177,10 +2177,12 @@ def _mla_fp8_prefill_attn(
         #
         # Exact, not approximate: after kv_b_proj gqa_ratio is 1, so q, k and v
         # all carry num_heads heads and attention is independent per head.
-        # Padding all three identically makes padded head j a duplicate of real
-        # head j % num_heads, so the real heads [0:num_heads] are bit-identical
-        # to the unpadded result. Same argument as the decode path; only the
-        # target width differs.
+        # Padding all three identically makes every padded head a duplicate of
+        # a real head, so the real heads are bit-identical to the unpadded
+        # result. get_mla_padded_q repeat_interleaves when the target is a
+        # multiple of num_heads (real heads at stride target // num_heads) and
+        # tiles otherwise (real heads [0:num_heads]). Same argument as the
+        # decode path; only the target width differs.
         _real_nhead = self.num_heads
         nhead = AiterMLAHelper.get_fp8_prefill_num_heads(_real_nhead)
         _pad = nhead != _real_nhead
@@ -2268,7 +2270,12 @@ def _mla_fp8_prefill_attn(
         )
 
         if _pad:
-            out.view(total_q, _real_nhead, v_head_dim).copy_(out_3d[:, :_real_nhead, :])
+            real_out = (
+                out_3d[:, :: nhead // _real_nhead, :]
+                if nhead % _real_nhead == 0
+                else out_3d[:, :_real_nhead, :]
+            )
+            out.view(total_q, _real_nhead, v_head_dim).copy_(real_out)
 
     def forward_mha(
         self,
